Text:
‎{{c1::بِـ}}

Transliteration: {{c1::bi}}

{{c2::in}} — Levantine; prefixed to the next word
Back Extra:
Cue: MSA — none; bi is shaami, her own dialect (the course tests Formal)

Why: baa.

Ex: Also the same bi- she later uses in ahlan bika (9/1): 'bi is a preposition like fii'.

Class: 8/27

Cue: MSA — -hu / ismuhu

Why: haa | alif + siin + miim + haa.

Ex: Rule: put a Damma (u) on the last letter of the noun, then add -hu: ism -> ismu -> ismuhu.

Ex: 'Those need a lot of practice, guys, because they're totally different from English.' She compared it to how hard English possessives were for her.

Ex: '-ii' = my, '-uka / -uki' = your, now '-uhu' = his and '-uhaa' = her.

Pitfall: she called this REQUIRED.

Ex: shaami (her dialect) — -o / ismo [sound:arabic_lingco_u4vs_18.mp3]

Class: 9/24, 9/29
